text: simulab generates wide variety data, different shapes, sample sizes, distributions parameters. parameters either drawn random set advance, cases stored data, known, recoverable testable. package designed simulation, evaluation statistical methods, training testing models software, learning teaching. Data generated specified parameters describe real persons, can shared, published given class without consent, review access agreements real data people require. generators cover declared variables treatment assignment, missing values copula dependence; group comparisons, regression Gaussian clusters; latent profile, latent class, factor item response models; multilevel, growth vector autoregressive longitudinal data; survival times censoring competing risks; sequences states Markov chains, hidden Markov models mixtures; behavioral event data; transition networks; random, bipartite, multiplex temporal networks. package written base R requires R 4.1.0 later. documentation, methodological guide reference every function, https://pak.dynasite.org/simulab/.

title: Combine survival definitions into a specification — define_survivals
code: # One call, named arguments, one row per event. define_survivals(   event   = c("time_relapse", "time_death"),   formula = c(-8, -9),   shape   = 0.3 ) #>          event formula scale shape transition #> 1   time_death      -9     1   0.3          0 #> 2 time_relapse      -8     1   0.3          0  # A piecewise hazard is two rows for one event. define_survivals(   event      = c("time", "time"),   formula    = c(-8, -6),   shape      = 0.3,   transition = c(0, 50) ) #>   event formula scale shape transition #> 1  time      -8     1   0.3          0 #> 2  time      -6     1   0.3         50  # Definitions built one at a time are still accepted. define_survivals(   define_survival("time_relapse", formula = -8, shape = 0.3),   define_survival("time_death", formula = -9, shape = 0.3) ) #>          event formula scale shape transition #> 1 time_relapse      -8     1   0.3          0 #> 2   time_death      -9     1   0.3          0  # Hazard calls. The log rate is an expression over the covariates. define_survivals(   time_relapse = hazard(log_rate = -8 + 0.5 * treatment, shape = 0.3),   time_death   = hazard(log_rate = -9, shape = 0.3) ) #>          event              formula scale shape transition #> 1   time_death                   -9     1   0.3          0 #> 2 time_relapse -8 + 0.5 * treatment     1   0.3          0  # A repeated event name is a piecewise hazard: the rate rises after day 60. define_survivals(   time = hazard(log_rate = -8, shape = 0.3),   time = hazard(log_rate = -5, shape = 0.3, from = 60) ) #>   event formula scale shape transition #> 1  time      -8     1   0.3          0 #> 2  time      -5     1   0.3         60

The variable name is the argument name. define_variables(   age     = normal(mean = 50, sd = 10),   treated = binary(prob = 0.5),   outcome = normal(mean = 10 + 0.2 * age + 2 * treated, sd = 2) ) #>   variable distribution parameter                        value #> 1      age       normal      mean                           50 #> 2      age       normal        sd                           10 #> 3  treated       binary      prob                          0.5 #> 4  outcome       normal      mean 10 + 0.2 * age + 2 * treated #> 5  outcome       normal        sd                            2  # Parameters may be positional, in the order list_distributions() reports. define_variables(y = normal(5, 1), count = poisson(3)) #>   variable distribution parameter value #> 1        y       normal      mean     5 #> 2        y       normal        sd     1 #> 3    count      poisson    lambda     3  # Specification columns. `formula` is the mean or linear predictor and may # refer to variables defined earlier. `variance` is a variance, not a # standard deviation. define_variables(   variable     = c("baseline", "treatment", "outcome"),   formula      = c("0", "0.5", "0.4 * baseline + 0.8 * treatment"),   variance     = c("1", "0", "1"),   distribution = c("normal", "binary", "normal") ) #>    variable distribution                          formula variance     link #> 1  baseline       normal                                0        1 identity #> 2 treatment       binary                              0.5        0 identity #> 3   outcome       normal 0.4 * baseline + 0.8 * treatment        1 identity  # A column given once is recycled, so a specification that shares one # distribution stays short. define_variables(   variable = c("x1", "x2", "x3"),   formula  = "0",   variance = "1" ) #>   variable distribution formula variance     link #> 1       x1       normal       0        1 identity #> 2       x2       normal       0        1 identity #> 3       x3       normal       0        1 identity  # Definitions built one at a time are still accepted. define_variables(   define_variable("age", formula = 40, variance = 100, distribution = "normal"),   define_variable("treated", formula = 0.5, distribution = "binary") ) #>   variable distribution formula variance     link #> 1      age       normal      40      100 identity #> 2  treated       binary     0.5        0 identity

title: Simulate a common-factor model — simulate_factors
text: Draws factor scores multivariate normal unit variances correlation factor_correlation, forms indicator intercept + loadings %*% scores + error, error standard deviation sqrt(uniqueness). implied population covariance loadings %*% factor_correlation %*% t(loadings) + diag(uniquenesses). factors unit variance, loadings standardized-factor metric.

title: Simulate a common-factor model — simulate_factors
text: n Number observations. single whole number least 2. loadings Variable--factor loading matrix (one row per indicator, one column per factor, least 2 rows), tidy data frame columns item, factor loading. Row column names, present, name indicators factors. uniquenesses Residual variances (standard deviations), scalar recycled across indicators one non-negative value per indicator. NULL (default) uses 1 - rowSums(loadings^2), gives every indicator unit total variance, loadings fully standardized. Loadings whose squared row sum exceeds one therefore raise error rather producing Heywood case. factor_correlation Optional factor correlation matrix, tidy data frame columns row, column correlation. NULL (default) makes factors orthogonal. intercepts Variable intercepts, scalar recycled across indicators (default, 0) one value per indicator. include_scores Single flag; TRUE true factor scores appended primary data one column per factor. Defaults FALSE. seed Optional random seed. batch Optional single positive whole number. given, simulator runs batch times returns plain list batch results, exactly call without batch returns. seed, every dataset gets seed drawn seed, whole batch reproducible; without one datasets consecutive draws session's random-number stream. default NULL returns single result.

title: Simulate longitudinal growth trajectories — simulate_growth
text: Draws per-unit random growth coefficients, forms outcome measurement occasion (intercept + b0) + (slope + b1) * time + (quadratic + b2) * time^2 plus normal residual noise, b2 present random_sd three elements. Every unit observed every occasion (balanced design).

title: Simulate longitudinal growth trajectories — simulate_growth
code: simulate_growth(   n,   times,   intercept = 0,   slope = 1,   quadratic = 0,   random_sd = c(1, 0.25),   random_correlation = NULL,   residual_sd = 1,   seed = NULL,   batch = NULL )

title: Simulate longitudinal growth trajectories — simulate_growth
text: n Number units. single whole number least 2. times Measurement occasions: finite numeric vector least two unique values, used verbatim time predictor (0:4 puts intercept first occasion). intercept, slope, quadratic Fixed growth coefficients, single number; default 0, 1 0. random_sd Standard deviations random intercept, slope, optional quadratic term. non-negative numeric vector length 2 (default, c(1, 0.25)) 3. random_correlation Correlation matrix random effects, matching length random_sd, tidy data frame columns row, column correlation. NULL (default) makes random effects uncorrelated. residual_sd Residual standard deviation. single positive number, defaulting 1. seed Optional random seed. batch Optional single positive whole number. given, simulator runs batch times returns plain list batch results, exactly call without batch returns. seed, every dataset gets seed drawn seed, whole batch reproducible; without one datasets consecutive draws session's random-number stream. default NULL returns single result.

title: Simulate longitudinal growth trajectories — simulate_growth
text: long-form simulab_sim base data.frame one row per unit-occasion (n * length(times) rows) columns id, time outcome. Rows ordered occasion first unit second. parameters component holds one row intercept, slope, quadratic residual_sd, columns term value (note residual_sd standard deviation, random-effect standard deviations repeated ). random_effects component holds one row per unit columns id, intercept, slope , random_sd three elements, quadratic, giving unit's deviation fixed coefficients.

title: Simulate item-response data — simulate_irt
text: simulab_sim base data.frame one row per respondent columns id one integer column per item, coded 0/1 dichotomous models 0 number thresholds model = "graded". abilities component holds one row per respondent columns id one true ability per dimension. parameters component holds one row per item dichotomous models, columns item, parameter ("difficulty"), category (NA), value, discrimination guessing; model = "graded" holds one row per item--threshold combination, parameter equal "threshold", category threshold index, guessing column.

title: Simulate item-response data — simulate_irt
text: dichotomous models probability correct response guessing + (1 - guessing) * plogis(discrimination * (theta - difficulty)), difficulty ability scale (point inflection), intercept. "rasch" fixes discriminations one "2pl" sets guessing zero; "3pl" uses guessing. model = "graded" cumulative category probabilities plogis(discrimination * (theta - threshold)) threshold item, category probabilities successive differences, thresholds also ability scale.

title: Simulate a latent class model — simulate_lca
code: # `probabilities` is a class x indicator x category array. Values fill the # class dimension fastest, so each pair below is one category across the two # classes: P(indicator = 1) then P(indicator = 2). probabilities <- array(   c(0.8, 0.2,   0.7, 0.3,     # category 1, for each class and indicator     0.2, 0.8,   0.3, 0.7),    # category 2, for each class and indicator   dim = c(2, 2, 2),   dimnames = list(     class = c("Class 1", "Class 2"),     indicator = c("item_1", "item_2"),     category = c("no", "yes")   ) )  # Only the `indicator` dimnames name the output columns, so the class and # category labels are passed explicitly. result <- simulate_lca(   n = 200,   probabilities = probabilities,   proportions = c(0.6, 0.4),   category_labels = c("no", "yes"),   seed = 1 ) head(result) #> <simulab_sim:lca> 6 rows x 4 columns #>   id latent_class item_1 item_2 #> 1  1      Class 1     no     no #> 2  2      Class 1     no     no #> 3  3      Class 1     no    yes #> 4  4      Class 2    yes     no #> 5  5      Class 1     no    yes #> 6  6      Class 2    yes     no #>  #> Truth (parameters): #>   latent_class indicator category probability proportion #> 1      Class 1    item_1       no         0.8        0.6 #> 2      Class 2    item_1       no         0.2        0.4 #> 3      Class 1    item_2       no         0.7        0.6 #> 4      Class 2    item_2       no         0.3        0.4 #> 5      Class 1    item_1      yes         0.2        0.6 #> 6      Class 2    item_1      yes         0.8        0.4 #> 7      Class 1    item_2      yes         0.3        0.6 #> 8      Class 2    item_2      yes         0.7        0.4 as.data.frame(result, what = "parameters") #>   latent_class indicator category probability proportion #> 1      Class 1    item_1       no         0.8        0.6 #> 2      Class 2    item_1       no         0.2        0.4 #> 3      Class 1    item_2       no         0.7        0.6 #> 4      Class 2    item_2       no         0.3        0.4 #> 5      Class 1    item_1      yes         0.2        0.6 #> 6      Class 2    item_1      yes         0.8        0.4 #> 7      Class 1    item_2      yes         0.3        0.6 #> 8      Class 2    item_2      yes         0.7        0.4

what: Simulate a multivariate longitudinal VAR process — simulate_longitudinal
title: Simulate a multivariate longitudinal VAR process — simulate_longitudinal
text: Draws person mean unit between_covariance around grand_means, runs first-order vector autoregression deviations person mean: y_t = mu + intercept + transition %*% (y_{t-1} - mu) + e_t, e_t drawn innovation_covariance. first burn_in occasions discarded retained occasions near stationarity.

title: Simulate a multivariate longitudinal VAR process — simulate_longitudinal
code: simulate_longitudinal(   n,   occasions,   transition,   intercept = 0,   innovation_covariance = NULL,   initial_covariance = NULL,   between_covariance = NULL,   grand_means = 0,   beeps_per_day = NULL,   burn_in = 50L,   seed = NULL,   batch = NULL )

title: Simulate a multivariate longitudinal VAR process — simulate_longitudinal
text: n Number units. single positive whole number. occasions Number occasions retained per unit. single whole number least 2. transition Lag-one coefficients square matrix, tidy data frame columns , coefficient (supplies matrix row column). Entry [, j] multiplies variable j previous occasion forming variable current occasion, rows index receiving variable columns predicting variable. spectral radius must one. intercept Variable intercepts, scalar recycled across variables (default, 0) one value per variable. intercept added deviation person mean every occasion, non-zero intercept shifts stationary mean person_mean + solve(diag(p) - transition) %*% intercept person_means component longer realized process mean. innovation_covariance Innovation covariance matrix, tidy data frame columns row, column covariance. Must symmetric positive semidefinite. NULL (default) uses identity. initial_covariance Initial-state covariance matrix, tidy data frame columns row, column covariance. NULL (default) reuses innovation_covariance. between_covariance -unit covariance person means, tidy data frame columns row, column covariance. NULL (default) zero matrix, giving every unit person mean, grand_means. grand_means Population means, scalar recycled across variables (default, 0) one value per variable. beeps_per_day Optional number occasions per day; occasions must divisible . Adds day beep columns returned data. Temporal carryover resets day boundary. burn_in Warm-occasions generated discarded output. single non-negative whole number, defaulting 50. seed Optional random seed. batch Optional single positive whole number. given, simulator runs batch times returns plain list batch results, exactly call without batch returns. seed, every dataset gets seed drawn seed, whole batch reproducible; without one datasets consecutive draws session's random-number stream. default NULL returns single result.

title: Simulate a multivariate longitudinal VAR process — simulate_longitudinal
text: long-form simulab_sim base data.frame one row per unit-occasion (n * occasions rows) columns id, occasion one per variable, plus day beep beeps_per_day supplied. Components: wide (one row per unit, one <variable>.<occasion> column per measurement), transition, innovation_covariance between_covariance (tidy matrix tables columns row, column coefficient covariance), person_means (one row per unit columns id one per variable).

title: Simulate a multivariate longitudinal VAR process — simulate_longitudinal
code: # `transition` is the lag-one coefficient matrix of the VAR process. result <- simulate_longitudinal(   n = 20,   occasions = 30,   transition = matrix(c(0.5, 0.1, 0.0, 0.4), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),   seed = 1 ) head(result) #> <simulab_sim:longitudinal_var> 6 rows x 4 columns #>   id occasion  variable_1 variable_2 #> 1  1        1 -0.77084247 -2.1925817 #> 2  1        2 -0.14114900 -2.5420051 #> 3  1        3  0.42604399 -2.1327222 #> 4  1        4 -0.01764584  1.2340777 #> 5  1        5  1.75519038 -0.7926695 #> 6  1        6  0.81688808  0.1331193 #>  #> Truth (transition): #>          row     column coefficient #> 1 variable_1 variable_1         0.5 #> 2 variable_2 variable_1         0.0 #> 3 variable_1 variable_2         0.1 #> 4 variable_2 variable_2         0.4 #>  #> Other tables: wide, innovation_covariance, between_covariance, person_means. Read one with as.data.frame(x, what = "wide"). components(result) #>                   table rows columns #> 1                  data  600       4 #> 2                  wide   20      61 #> 3            transition    4       3 #> 4 innovation_covariance    4       3 #> 5    between_covariance    4       3 #> 6          person_means   20       3

what: Simulate a two-level latent profile model — simulate_ml_lpa
title: Simulate a two-level latent profile model — simulate_ml_lpa
text: Draws data nonparametric two-level mixture Vermunt (2003). Every cluster belongs latent cluster class, cluster class fixes common individual profile inside clusters, profiles share one measurement model across every cluster. Cluster classes therefore differ profile prevalence, profile means, separates design simulating one latent profile model per cluster.

title: Simulate a two-level latent profile model — simulate_ml_lpa
code: simulate_ml_lpa(   clusters,   cluster_size,   means,   profile_probabilities,   sds = 1,   cluster_class_proportions = NULL,   correlations = NULL,   labels = NULL,   cluster_class_labels = NULL,   seed = NULL,   batch = NULL )

title: Simulate a two-level latent profile model — simulate_ml_lpa

Column names become indicator columns returned data; row names, profile values tidy table, name profiles unless labels given. profile_probabilities Cluster-class--profile matrix profile prevalences (one row per cluster class, one column per profile), tidy data frame columns cluster_class, profile probability. Every value must positive row rescaled sum one. single row gives ordinary latent profile model observed clusters. sds Scalar (default, 1), per-variable vector, profile--variable matrix, tidy data frame columns profile, variable sd. values must positive. measurement model shared every cluster class, standard deviations vary across . cluster_class_proportions Cluster-class proportions, one positive value per cluster class; rescaled sum one. title: Simulate a two-level latent profile model — simulate_ml_lpa
text: Vermunt, J. K. (2003). Multilevel latent class models. Sociological Methodology, 33, 213–239. doi:10.1111/j.0081-1750.2003.t01-1-00131.x

title: Simulate a two-level latent profile model — simulate_ml_lpa

Read one with as.data.frame(x, what = "profile_probabilities"). as.data.frame(result, what = "profile_probabilities") #>   cluster_class   profile probability cluster_class_proportion #> 1       Class 1 Profile 1         0.6                      0.5 #> 2       Class 2 Profile 1         0.1                      0.5 #> 3       Class 1 Profile 2         0.3                      0.5 #> 4       Class 2 Profile 2         0.3                      0.5 #> 5       Class 1 Profile 3         0.1                      0.5 #> 6       Class 2 Profile 3         0.6                      0.5 as.data.frame(result, what = "clusters") #>    cluster cluster_class size #> 1        1       Class 2   20 #> 2        2       Class 2   20 #> 3        3       Class 1   20 #> 4        4       Class 1   20 #> 5        5       Class 2   20 #> 6        6       Class 1   20 #> 7        7       Class 1   20 #> 8        8       Class 1   20 #> 9        9       Class 1   20 #> 10      10       Class 2   20 #> 11      11       Class 2   20 #> 12      12       Class 2   20 #> 13      13       Class 1   20 #> 14      14       Class 2   20 #> 15      15       Class 1   20 #> 16      16       Class 2   20 #> 17      17       Class 1   20 #> 18      18       Class 1   20 #> 19      19       Class 2   20 #> 20      20       Class 1   20 #> 21      21       Class 1   20 #> 22      22       Class 2   20 #> 23      23       Class 1   20 #> 24      24       Class 2   20 #> 25      25       Class 2   20 #> 26      26       Class 2   20 #> 27      27       Class 2   20 #> 28      28       Class 2   20 #> 29      29       Class 1   20 #> 30      30       Class 2   20

title: Simulate a two-level Gaussian model — simulate_multilevel
text: clusters Number clusters. single whole number least 2. cluster_size Units per cluster: single whole number recycled across clusters, one whole number per cluster, clusters may unbalanced. intercept Fixed intercept. single number, defaulting 0. slopes Named fixed-effect slopes; names become predictor columns returned data. Defaults numeric(0), intercept-model predictor columns. predictor_means, predictor_sds Mean standard deviation predictor, scalar recycled across predictors (defaults, 0 1) one value per entry slopes. Predictors drawn independently unit level, cluster level, carry -cluster variance construction. random_intercept_sd Random-intercept standard deviation. single non-negative number, defaulting 1. random_slope_sd Random-slope standard deviation first predictor ; remaining predictors fixed slopes. single non-negative number, defaulting 0 (random slope). random_effect_correlation Correlation random intercept slope. single number [-1, 1], defaulting 0. residual_sd Residual standard deviation. single positive number, defaulting 1. seed Optional random seed. batch Optional single positive whole number. given, simulator runs batch times returns plain list batch results, exactly call without batch returns. seed, every dataset gets seed drawn seed, whole batch reproducible; without one datasets consecutive draws session's random-number stream. default NULL returns single result.

text: simulab_sim base data.frame one row per unit (sum(cluster_size) rows) columns id, cluster, one column per name slopes, outcome. Components: fixed_effects (one row per fixed term, columns term coefficient), variance_components (one row random_intercept, random_slope residual, columns component variance – squared standard deviations supplied arguments), random_effects (one row per cluster, columns cluster, random_intercept random_slope; random_slope column present zero random_slope_sd = 0).

what: Simulate proportional-hazards survival data with calibrated censoring — simulate_proportional_survival
title: Simulate proportional-hazards survival data with calibrated censoring — simulate_proportional_survival
text: Draws independent covariates, multiplies baseline cumulative hazard exp(x %*% coefficients), inverts event time, model proportional hazards coefficient log hazard ratio. three baselines , unit linear predictor eta, Weibull H(t) = rate * exp(eta) * t^shape, exponential H(t) = rate * exp(eta) * t, Gompertz H(t) = rate * exp(eta) * (exp(shape * t) - 1) / shape. Censoring random, administrative: independent exponential censoring time drawn every unit, rate solved expected censored fraction equals censoring.

title: Simulate proportional-hazards survival data with calibrated censoring — simulate_proportional_survival
code: simulate_proportional_survival(   n,   coefficients,   baseline = c("weibull", "exponential", "gompertz"),   rate = 0.1,   shape = 1,   censoring = 0.3,   covariate_distribution = c("normal", "binary"),   seed = NULL,   batch = NULL )

title: Simulate proportional-hazards survival data with calibrated censoring — simulate_proportional_survival
text: n Sample size. single whole number least 5. coefficients Covariate log-hazard coefficients, numeric vector least one element one entry per covariate. names become covariate columns; unnamed vectors named X1, X2, . baseline Baseline hazard family, one "weibull" (default), "exponential" "gompertz". rate Positive scale factor baseline cumulative hazard. single positive number, defaulting 0.1. constant hazard baseline "exponential". shape Positive shape Weibull Gompertz baseline, textbook parameterization formulas (hazard rises time shape 1 Weibull baseline). single positive number, defaulting 1. ignored exponential baseline. censoring Target fraction censored observations. single number [0, 1), defaulting 0.3. Exactly 0 turns censoring every observation event; realized fraction random around target otherwise. covariate_distribution Distribution covariates drawn , independently, one "normal" (default, standard normal) "binary" (Bernoulli probability 0.5). seed Optional random seed. single number, NULL (default). batch Optional single positive whole number. given, simulator runs batch times returns plain list batch results, exactly call without batch returns. seed, every dataset gets seed drawn seed, whole batch reproducible; without one datasets consecutive draws session's random-number stream. default NULL returns single result.

Components: parameters (one row per term, columns term value, holding coefficients followed baseline_rate, shape solved censoring_rate) diagnostics (one row, columns target_censoring, realized_censoring baseline).

title: Compare recovered estimates with known simulation truth — validate_recovery
code: estimates <- data.frame(term = c("x1", "x2"), estimate = c(0.52, -0.28)) truth <- data.frame(term = c("x1", "x2"), truth = c(0.5, -0.3)) validate_recovery(estimates, truth, tolerance = 0.1) #>   term estimate truth bias absolute_error relative_error recovered #> 1   x1     0.52   0.5 0.02           0.02     0.04000000      TRUE #> 2   x2    -0.28  -0.3 0.02           0.02    -0.06666667      TRUE  # One data set: the fitted model against the result's own truth. data_set <- simulate_regression(seed = 1) validate_recovery(lm(outcome ~ x1 + x2, data = data_set), data_set) #>          term   estimate truth         bias absolute_error relative_error #> 1 (Intercept) -0.6252180 -0.63  0.004782022    0.004782022   -0.007590511 #> 2          x1  0.1652958  0.15  0.015295795    0.015295795    0.101971968 #> 3          x2  0.7541006  0.82 -0.065899429    0.065899429   -0.080365157 #>   recovered #> 1      TRUE #> 2      TRUE #> 3      TRUE  # A batch with drawn coefficients: each data set is compared with its own. datasets <- simulate_regression(seed = 1, batch = 20) fit_coefficients <- function(data) {   fit <- lm(outcome ~ x1 + x2, data = data)   data.frame(term = names(coef(fit)), estimate = unname(coef(fit))) } estimates <- apply_batch(datasets, fit_coefficients) head(validate_recovery(estimates, datasets)) #>   batch_id        term   estimate truth        bias absolute_error #> 1        1 (Intercept)  0.4871271  0.52 -0.03287288     0.03287288 #> 2        1          x1  0.4291198  0.46 -0.03088022     0.03088022 #> 3        1          x2 -0.4881249 -0.34 -0.14812486     0.14812486 #> 4        2 (Intercept) -0.5419140 -0.53 -0.01191397     0.01191397 #> 5        2          x1  0.4818146  0.45  0.03181463     0.03181463 #> 6        2          x2  0.5997644  0.76 -0.16023560     0.16023560 #>   relative_error recovered #> 1    -0.06321708      TRUE #> 2    -0.06713092      TRUE #> 3     0.43566136     FALSE #> 4     0.02247919      TRUE #> 5     0.07069917      TRUE #> 6    -0.21083632     FALSE
